results.name: ldCorrelationDecayHyperbolic
results.source: the rate slot lambda*sqrt(fstGap) IDENTIFIED as 4*Ne*c, zero fitted constants
results.note: the oracle is the freely fitted rate of the body's own shape; the prediction is the identification under test; positive control 'PANMICTIC Ne=2000, within-population sigma_d^2 decay rate through the identical estimator and fit' passed at 0.37 sems
results.regime: two-deme island model at migration-drift equilibrium, 4 Mb, recombination and mutation both 1e-8 and IDENTICAL in every cell, 300 haplotypes per deme, 8 replicates. Six cells cross Ne over {1000,2000,4000} with two migration levels, so realised F_ST forms two clusters at every Ne and Ne is not confounded with F_ST. The oracle is the rate that makes the Ohta-Kimura shape fit that cell's measured cross-deme Corr(D) curve, with the amplitude fitted because both bodies assert an amplitude of 1 that the measurement rejects. Corr(D) is split-half over disjoint haplotype halves in each deme, so its attenuation is not distance-dependent. F_ST is the realised Hudson value on the MAF-filtered sites the curve is measured on, never the nominal 1/(1+4Nm), which a pilot showed is badly wrong for two demes

results.name: ldCorrelationDecayHyperbolic [the amplitude at zero distance, which both bodies fix at 1, competing]
results.source: the normalisation asserts Corr(D) -> 1 as distance -> 0
results.note: at zero recombination distance D is inherited from the ancestor and then drifts independently in the two demes, so there is no reason for the cross-deme correlation to be 1; positive control 'PANMICTIC Ne=2000, within-population sigma_d^2 decay rate through the identical estimator and fit' passed at 0.37 sems
